description: The single declarative source of capability routing for the fleet: which capability a unit of work needs, which registered persona owns it, which FinOps tier that persona runs at, and the risk floor that outranks both. `fleet/routing.py` is its only reader and `fleet/brain.py` consults that module — the brain keeps no second copy of this dialect (ADR-0012).

provenance.doctrine: GR-10 — a harvested asset records its source, path, verdict and landing. The vendored module is pinned read-only and never edited (GR-5); no source file was copied, so no `harvested_from` marker is required — this policy re-implements the pattern and reuses the vocabulary.

harvested_from.asset: the declared routing contract this policy consumes: features capability-registry, task-routing, model-tiering, escalation
harvested_from.landing: this file (capabilities / personas / finops / risk / escalation)

harvested_from.asset: capability -> agent resolution from capability metadata
tier assignment, escalation-as-a-floor, escalate once on observed difficulty
the dispatched hermes persona: capabilitySet [code-author, test-author, test-run, memory-ops] at defaultModelTier MED
harvested_from.landing: personas.hermes — the loader verifies this card's tier and capability set against the policy

harvested_from.asset: the dispatched paperclip persona: capabilitySet [research, docs-authoring, memory-ops] at defaultModelTier LOW
harvested_from.landing: personas.paperclip — the loader verifies this card's tier and capability set against the policy

harvested_from.asset: the closed capability vocabulary (capabilities{} keys) this policy's ids are drawn from

code-author.summary: Author code changes and pull requests.

test-run.summary: Execute gates and verification and return real evidence.

memory-ops.summary: Read/write scoped memory (repository, session, user). Declared by both cards; routed once, to the knowledge assistant (see shared_capabilities).

module-brief.summary: Compose each mandatory module's distributable brief from the module registry, the committed board snapshot and the hub catalog (ADR-0012 reporting half; issue #447).

unrouted_capabilities.orchestrate: the brain itself plans, decomposes and dispatches; no registered persona declares this capability
unrouted_capabilities.task-claim: claiming is dispatch bookkeeping (governance/dispatch), not a persona capability
unrouted_capabilities.security-review: security work runs under the risk floor below; no registered persona declares this capability
unrouted_capabilities.architecture-decision: decisions-only advisor work; no registered persona declares this capability
unrouted_capabilities.infra-authoring: production-IaC work runs under the risk floor below; no registered persona declares this capability
unrouted_capabilities.audit: independent verification is a posture, not a dispatch target, at this phase
unrouted_capabilities.finops-meter: metering is the observability pillar's job, not a dispatched persona's
unrouted_capabilities.data-analysis: no registered persona declares this capability at this phase

finops.note: Hermes' LOW/MED/HIGH (and MAX) persona tiers map onto this repo's harvested FinOps vocabulary (governance/finops/policy.json: tiers flash|pro|auditor). The thinking effort is the tier's floor of care: flash runs thinking-off, pro runs low, auditor runs high. tier_map and thinking must agree with the tiers the wire enforces (fleet/channel.py) — fleet/tests/test_routing.py is the parity gate.
finops.rule: start cheap, escalate once on observed difficulty; the operator may raise a tier, never lower a floor

high_floor.rule: security, secrets, auth, identity and production-IaC work never starts below this floor. The floor outranks the persona tier, applies whatever capability the work claims, and is a floor — never a ceiling.

escalation.rule: escalate once, on observed difficulty — never speculatively and never pre-emptively
escalation.requires: a reason naming the observed difficulty
never: downgrade a tier or a thinking level
escalate more than one rung at a time
